node.label: David Harvey
node.date_label: Social Justice and the City (1973) · The Condition of Postmodernity (1989) · “The Right to the City” (2008)
node.description: Connects urbanization and capitalist accumulation with questions of collective power over the city. The opening of his 2008 essay defines the right to the city as a collective capacity to reshape urbanization rather than merely individual access to existing resources. His selected 1989 discussion links place identity, tradition and flexible accumulation while allowing that regional resistance can have value without providing a sufficient programme of radical change. Doreen Massey’s named 1995 criticism contests that treatment of tradition and the possibilities of place. The entry presents a disputed spatial argument, rather than treating either position as a consensus of geographers or urban historians.
